RTGS was introduced in India in 2004 by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to facilitate the transfer of large sums of money between banks. The system is designed to provide a fast, secure, and reliable way to transfer funds, with the ability to settle transactions in real-time, 24/7, 365 days a year.

In the RTGS system, transactions are settled in real-time, meaning that the payment is credited to the beneficiary's account immediately after the payment instruction is received by the RBI. This system is used for high-value transactions, typically above a certain threshold, and is used by banks to transfer funds between themselves.

RTGS is an important system for facilitating large transactions, such as corporate payments, government transactions, and other high-value transactions, and is considered a reliable and efficient way to transfer funds between banks.
